It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. A Romanian supermarket which was ordered to close will be allowed to reopen from later this week. Suffolk Police believe that Magazin Bacau Romanian Supermarket, located at 51 Buttermarket is no longer associated with criminal behaviour or antisocial behaviour and therefore can reopen from Saturday, August 8. Ipswich Magistrates' Court approved a three-month closure notice for the store in May, with it set to expire on Saturday, August 8. The closure notice was issued in May of this year (Image: Oli Picton) Suffolk Police raised concerns that the store was associated with criminal behaviour and antisocial behaviour and a led a multi-agency investigation. With the three month closure order set to expire, the police have confirmed that they have no applied to extend the closure notice. Suffolk Police said: "The closure order was initially granted for a period of three months. Police have not applied for an extension, and there is currently no evidence to suggest the premises will continue to be associated with serious nuisance, disorder, criminal behaviour or antisocial behaviour. "The business owner has complied with the conditions of the closure and has chosen to reopen the business while continuing to seek advice and guidance from Suffolk police. "Officers have maintained regular contact with the owner and will conduct regular visits to ensure there are no further issues once the premises reopens. "We will also continue to work with neighbouring businesses and Ipswich Borough Council to maintain community confidence." The illegal alcohol was seized by Suffolk Police (Image: Suffolk police) A warrant executed on November 10, 2025, led to the seizure of illicit alcohol, tobacco and prescription-only medication. The alcohol was suspected of being sold illegally to groups gathering outside and contributing to anti-social behaviour in the area. Evidence had been gathered by Suffolk Police over many months after fears of "prolonged and persistent" anti-social behaviour. However, Ipswich Magistrates' Court overturned the initial closure notice, and the shop was then allowed to reopen.
